name: Mystic (AVV)
body:
Gypsies, fortunetellers, hedge wizards, hags, crones, and court magicians may all be considered mystics. Many live in towns or cities, selling their services to the masses, while others keep their practice secret. Some mystics avoid civilization completely and live as hermits in remote caves, shunning all visitors.

Masters of the esoteric arts, arcane secrets, and the outer worlds, mystics are skilled at interpreting fate and may shape destiny with their magic. The power of the mystic is subtle but profound. They often mix true sorcery with senseless rituals and the antics of a charlatan, confusing anyone who would learn their secrets by observation.

Role: While some mystics are recluses, living on the edge of civilization, others live within society, openly or in hiding. And there are those that travel the world as vagabonds, seeking greater understanding of the mysterious powers that guide them. The mystic’s spells makes them adept at filling a number of different roles, from seer to healer, and their mystic powers grant them a number of abilities that are useful in a fight.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d6.

Class Skills

The mystic’s class skills are Craft (Int), Fly (Dex), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (history) (Int), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Knowledge (Religion), Linguistics (Int), Profession (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 2 + Int modifier.

Class Features

The following are the class features of the mystic.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Mystics are proficient with the club, dagger, gastraphetes, manuballista, and quarterstaff, but not with any type of armor or shield. Armor interferes with a mystic’s powers, which can cause her spells with somatic components to fail.

Mystic Skills (Ex)

Mystics are proficient in an array of esoteric skill uses not available to other PCs. These are not entirely new skills, but rather new uses of existing skills for those trained in the mystic arts. A character must be trained in the appropriate skill to use that skill’s unlock, even if the skill can normally be used untrained.

It’s impossible to take 10 for a mystic skill unlock. Mystic skill unlocks require intense concentration and strenuous effort, so the amount a character can use each skill unlock is limited to once per day or per week. This limit is for all uses of the skill unlock; if a character uses hypnotism to implant a suggestion, she can’t also use it to recall memories on the same day.

This section describes each new skill unlock and the typical DCs and modifiers for associated checks. Some new types of gear in this section grant bonuses on specific occult skill unlocks.

The mystic skill unlocks (and their associated skills) are:

Automatic Writing (Linguistics)
Dowsing (Survival)
Faith Healing (Heal)
Hypnotism (Diplomacy)
Object Reading (Appraise)
Prognostication (Sense Motive)
Read Aura (Perception)

Arcane Key: At 1st level, mystics obtain a key object that is instrumental to their arcane power. A mystic can use a key item to cast additional spells or to serve as a magical item. Without a key item, mystics have difficulty casting spells.

Mystics begin play with an arcane key at no cost.

Objects that are arcane keys must fall into one of the following categories: amulet, circlet, crystal ball, phylactery, ring, rod, scroll, staff, wand, or weapon.

These objects are always masterwork quality. Weapons acquired at 1st level are not made of any special material.

If the object is an amulet, circlet, phylactery, or ring, it must be worn to have effect, while crystals, rods, staves, scrolls, wands, and weapons must be held in one hand.

Scrolls may be etched in copper or clay, or written on sheepskin. Rarely is a key scroll made of papyrus.

If a mystic attempts to cast a spell without her key item worn or in hand, she must make a concentration check or lose the spell. The DC for this check is equal to 20 + the spell’s level. If the item is a circlet (or phylactery), ring, or amulet, it occupies the head, ring, or neck slot accordingly.

A key item can be used once per day to cast any one spell that the mystic has in her spellbook and is capable of casting, even if the spell is not prepared. This spell is treated like any other spell cast by the mystic, including casting time, duration, and other effects dependent on the mystic’s level. This spell cannot be modified by metamagic feats or other abilities.

A mystic can add additional magic abilities to her key item as if she has the required item creation feats and if she meets the level prerequisites of the feat. For example, a mystic with a dagger for a key item must be at least 5th level to add magic abilities to the dagger (see the Craft Magic Arms and Armor feat in Feats). If the key item is a wand, it loses its wand abilities when its last charge is consumed, but it is not destroyed and it retains all of its key item properties and can be used to craft a new wand. The magic properties of a key item, including any magic abilities added to the object, only function for the mystic who owns it. If a key item’s owner dies, or the object is replaced, the item reverts to being an ordinary masterwork item of the appropriate type.

If a key item is damaged, it is restored to full hit points the next time the mystic prepares her spells. If the key item is lost or destroyed, it can be replaced after 1 week in a special ritual that costs 200 gp per mystic level plus the cost of the masterwork item. This ritual takes 8 hours to complete. Items replaced in this way do not possess any of the additional enchantments of the previous key item. A mystic can designate an existing magic item as her bonded item. This functions in the same way as replacing a lost or destroyed item except that the new magic item retains its abilities while gaining the benefits and drawbacks of becoming a key item.

Mystic Power: At 4th level and every two levels thereafter, mystics gain a special mystic power, selected from the list below. Note that some mystic powers have minimum level requirements or prerequisites.

Change Shape (Sp)

With this power, a mystic can change her shape for a number of rounds per day equal to her mystic level. These rounds do not need to be consecutive. This ability otherwise functions like beast shape II or elemental body I. Mystics must be at least 8th level to select this power.

Diviner’s Fortune (Sp)

When a character activates this mystic power, she can touch any creature as a standard action to give it an insight bonus on all of its attack rolls, skill checks, ability checks, and saving throws equal to 1/2 her mystic level (minimum +1) for 1 round. Mystics can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + their Intelligence modifier.

Energy Absorption (Su)

A mystic with this power gains an amount of energy absorption equal to 3 times her mystic level per day. Whenever she takes energy damage, apply immunity, vulnerability (if any), and resistance first and apply the rest to this absorption, reducing the mystic’s daily total by that amount. Any damage in excess of the mystic’s absorption is applied to her normally.

Forewarned (Su)

Mystics with this power can always act in the surprise round even if they fail to make a Perception roll to notice a foe, but they are still considered flatfooted until they take an action. In addition, mystics with this power receive a bonus on initiative checks equal to 1/2 their mystic level (minimum +1).

Fortune (Su)

The mystic can grant a creature within 30 feet a bit of good luck for 1 round. The target can call upon this good luck once per round, allowing her to reroll any ability check, attack roll, saving throw, or skill check, taking the better result. She must decide to use this ability before the first roll is made. At 8th level, the duration of this power is extended by 1 round. Once a creature has benefited from this power, it cannot benefit from it again for 24 hours.

Healing (Su)

A mystic with this power can soothe the wounds of those she touches. This acts as a cure light wounds spell, using the mystic’s caster level. Once a creature has benefited from the healing power, it cannot benefit from it again for 24 hours. At 5th level, this power acts like cure moderate wounds.

Improved Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

A mystic with this power uses her foresight and precognition to prevent opponents from flanking her.

This power denies a rogue the ability to sneak attack the mystic by flanking her, unless the attacker has at least four more rogue levels than the target has mystic levels.

If a mystic already has uncanny dodge (see above) from another class, the levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum rogue level required to flank the mystic.

Misfortune (Su)

The mystic can cause a creature within 30 feet to suffer grave misfortune for 1 round.

Anytime the creature makes an ability check, attack roll, saving throw, or skill check, it must roll twice and take the worse result. A Will save negates this mystic power. At 8th level, the duration of this power is extended by 1 round. This mystic power affects all rolls the target must make while it lasts. Whether or not the save is successful, a creature cannot be the target of this mystic power again for 1 day.

Mystic’s Foresight (Su)

Mystics with this power gain a +1 dodge bonus to their AC for every two levels of mystic they have (max +5 at 10th level).

Physical Enhancement (Su)

Mystics with this power gain a +1 enhancement bonus to one physical ability score (Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution). This bonus increases by +1 for every five mystic levels she possesses to a maximum of +2 at 10th level. You can change this bonus to a new ability score when you prepare spells.

Protective Ward (Su)

As a standard action, mystics with this power can create a 10-foot-radius field of protective magic centered on them that lasts for a number of rounds equal to their Intelligence modifier.

All allies in this area (including the mystic) receive a +1 deflection bonus to their AC. This bonus increases by +1 for every five mystic levels the character possesses. Mystics may use this power a number of times per day equal to 3 + their Intelligence modifier.

Resistance (Ex)

Mystics with this power gain resistance 5 to an energy type of their choice, chosen when they prepare spells. This resistance can be changed each day.

Scrying Adept (Su)

Mystics with this power are always aware when they are being observed via magic, as if they had a permanent detect scrying. In addition, whenever they scry on a subject, treat the subject as one step more familiar to the mystic. Very familiar subjects get a –10 penalty on their save to avoid scrying attempts by mystics with this power.

Telekinetic Fist (Sp)

As a standard action mystics can strike with a telekinetic fist, targeting any foe within 30 feet as a ranged touch attack. The telekinetic fist deals 1d4 points of bludgeoning damage + 1 for every two mystic levels the character possesses.

Mystics may use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + their Intelligence modifier.

Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

A mystic with this power can feel the approach of danger before her senses would normally allow her to do so. She cannot be caught flat-footed, nor does she lose her Dex bonus to AC if the attacker is invisible. She still loses her Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. A mystic with this ability can still lose her Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action (see Combat) against her.

If a mystic already has uncanny dodge from a different class, she automatically gains improved uncanny dodge (see below) instead.

Ward (Su)

A mystic can use this power to place a protective ward over one creature. The warded creature receives a +2 deflection bonus to AC and a +2 resistance bonus on saving throws. This ward lasts until the warded creature is hit or fails a saving throw. A mystic knows when a warded creature is no longer protected. A mystic can have only one ward active at a time. If the mystic uses this ability again, the previous ward immediately ends. A mystic cannot use this ability on herself. At 8th level, the bonuses provided by this ward increase by +1.

Spellcasting

A mystic casts arcane spells drawn from the mystic spell list. A mystic must choose and prepare her spells ahead of time.

To learn, prepare, or cast a spell, the mystic must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a mystic’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the mystic’s Intelligence modifier.

A mystic can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Her base daily spell allotment is given on Table 3: The Mystic. In addition, she receives bonus spells per day if she has a high Intelligence score (see Ability Modifiers and Bonus Spells).

A mystic must choose and prepare her spells ahead of time by getting 8 hours of sleep and spending 1 hour studying her spellbook. While studying, the mystic decides which spells to prepare.

The mystic’s “spellbook” is not actually a bound book, but rather a scroll, or collection of scrolls, written on papyrus, copper, sheepskin, or even clay tablets.

Mystic Spell List

Mystics choose their spells from the following list.

0 Level Mystic Spells—arcane mark, create water, dancing lights, daze, detect magic, detect poison, ghost sound, guidance, light, mending, purify food and drink, read magic, stabilize, touch of fatigue.

1st Level Mystic Spells—animate rope, bless, cause fear, command, comprehend languages, cure light wounds, detect chaos, detect evil, detect good, detect law, detect secret doors, detect undead, divine favor, endure elements, hypnotism, identify, inflict light wounds, mage armor, magic weapon, mount, obscuring mist, protection from chaos, protection from evil, protection from good, protection from law, sleep, true strike, unseen servant.

2nd Level Mystic Spells—aid, animal trance, arcane lock, augury, bear’s endurance, blindness/deafness, bull’s strength, cat’s grace, cure moderate wounds, darkness, darkvision, daze monster, delay poison, detect thoughts, eagle’s splendor, enthrall, false life, fox’s cunning, gust of wind, hypnotic pattern, inflict moderate wounds, invisibility, knock, locate object, mirror image, object reading, obscure object, owl’s wisdom, protection from arrows, resist energy, rope trick, scorching ray, see invisibility, spider climb, web, whispering wind, zone of truth.

3rd Level Mystic Spells—animate dead, arcane sight, beast shape I, bestow curse, blindness/deafness, blink, clairaudience/clairvoyance, contagion continual flame, cure serious wounds, daylight, deeper darkness, deep slumber, dispel magic, fly, gaseous form, glyph of warding, greater magic weapon, neutralize poison, guiding star*, haste, heroism, inflict serious wounds, lightning bolt, locate object, magic circle, meld into stone, nondetection, phantom steed, rage, suggestion, protection from energy, remove blindness/deafness, slow, speak with dead, suggestion, tongues, water breathing, water walk.

4th Level Mystic Spells—arcane eye, beast shape II, cure critical wounds, detect scrying, dimensional anchor, dimension door, discern lies, divination, elemental body, geas (lesser), globe of invulnerability (lesser), inflict critical wounds, locate creature, magic weapon (greater), minor creation, planar ally (lesser), polymorph, rainbow pattern, scrying, secure shelter, stone shape, stoneskin, wall of fire.

5th Level Mystic Spells—baleful polymorph, banish, beast shape III, blight, break enchantment, commune, contact other plane, dismissal, dream, elemental body II, fabricate, mage’s faithful hound, mage’s private sanctum, magic jar, major creation, mark of justice, mind fog, nightmare, overland flight, planar binding (lesser), plane shift, plant shape I, prying eyes, raise dead, reincarnate, scrying, secret chest, seeming, spell resistance, symbol of pain, symbol of sleep, telekinesis, telepathic bond, teleport, transmute mud to rock/rock to mud, true seeing, wall of stone.
